newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian stocks end mostly lower, Hong Kong up.
newsitem.headline: Asian stocks end mostly lower, Hong Kong up.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks finished higher on Monday, but elsewhere in Asia shares fell, including in Tokyo where futures-related selling halted last week's strong gains. The 225-issue Nikkei average, after roaring ahead at the end of last week, lost 135.96 points or 0.64 percent to land at 21,065.08. Its December futures were 100 points lower at 21,100.
"There were hopes that the sharp gains made last week would be maintained, but arbitrage-linked selling dragged down the indices," said Akihiro Naemura, Okasan Securities strategist.
"Foreign investors are actually waiting for domestic investors to start buying and bring up the indices," a broker at a foreign securities house said.

He added that foreign investors were waiting for the Nikkei average to move out of its current boxed range and rise above the end-March level of 21,406, and that they were unlikely to revise their selling stance drastically until the day comes.
"Even after the Nikkei posted the year's fourth largest gain on Friday, it still had a percent or so to go," he said. On Friday, the benchmark thundered 429.93 points higher to 21,201.04.
Hong Kong stocks closed slightly up largely on speculative interest in Hongkong Telecom, brokers said.
"If you take out the six percent gain in Hongkong Telecom today, the index would have been down," said Claire Burges-Watson in institutional sales at Kim Eng Securities.
The Hang Seng Index finished 20.70 points up at 12,771.86 after recovering from an 80-point tumble at the start of the day.
Investors reacted positively after a London newspaper reported the Hong Kong phone company was likely to pass into Chinese hands. The company called the report "gossip".
But most of the market's recent leaders underwent some selling, suggesting the index could see a pullback on Tuesday.
"It should be a quiet day tomorrow. We are overdue for a bit of consolidation, said Lino Delgado, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
Taiwan share prices closed slightly lower as investors switched to the over-the-counter securities market, which has performed strongly in recent days, brokers said.
The index ended down 11.96 points or 0.18 percent at 6,571.12.
Korean stocks closed slightly down in volatile trading, brokers said.
"Buying sentiment was reviving in the belief the market has hit the bottom," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
The composite stock index closed 1.29 points lower at 729.53. It touched the year's new intra-day low of 720.01.
Profit-taking pulled the Jakarta index down despite increases in some heavily capitalised stocks, brokers said.
The composite index fell 0.89 points, or 0.15 percent, to 601.13 points after hitting a high for the day of 604.17 points. Losers led gainers by 71 to 46, with 53 counters unchanged.
A broker said the market was likely to continue its correction on Tuesday.
Thai stocks lost about two percent in afternoon trading as foreign and local investors continued taking profits on gains posted by communications and finance stocks last week, analysts said.
The SET Index declined about 20 points to 947.28.
The Malaysian and Singapore stock markets were closed for a Hindu festival and will reopen on Tuesday.
Crude oil futures went untraded, also due to the religious holiday. The SIMEX December contract was last quoted at $23.05/$23.15 against its Friday's close on London's IPE of $22.98 per barrel.
The dollar was lower in late Tokyo following a day of choppy trading. At 1115 GMT the dollar stood at 111.38/1.48 yen and 1.5040/50 marks.
Gold bullion ended slightly higher, finishing at $379.70/380.20 an ounce in Hong Kong against New York's US$379.20/70 close on Friday.
